summary:
The `scan_current_repository` now reports `findingCount: 0`, indicating that all baseline findings within the configured severity scope (CRITICAL, HIGH) are absent from the repository. The build command `mvn clean verify` also succeeds. All hard constraints, including the Spring Boot version policy and the prohibition of suppression files, have been met. No new CRITICAL or HIGH severity findings were introduced.

The resolution involved the following steps:
1.  Upgraded `org.apache.commons:commons-text` from `1.9` to `1.10.0` in the root `pom.xml`.
2.  Upgraded `org.json:json` from `20230227` to `20231013` in the root `pom.xml`.
3.  Upgraded `org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent` from `4.0.6` to `4.1.0` in the root `pom.xml` to address several transitive vulnerabilities.
4.  Added exclusions for `com.vaadin.external.google:android-json` from `org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-test` in `task-service/pom.xml` and `task-web/pom.xml` to resolve a dependency convergence warning.
5.  Explicitly declared `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core` with version `11.0.25` in the `dependencyManagement` section of the root `pom.xml` to fix remaining Tomcat vulnerabilities that were not resolved by the Spring Boot parent upgrade.

This sequence of changes successfully addressed all identified vulnerabilities and ensured the project remains buildable and compatible.
